title: Mating a lone king: queen, rook, and the stalemate trap
outcomes: Mates a bare king with queen or rook and king without stalemating it
Recognises checkmate, stalemate and neither at a glance
Checks, before every non-mating move, that the lone king still has a legal move and that the piece is safe

steps.text: To mate a bare king, a queen or rook alone is not enough: push the king to an edge and bring your own king close. Before every move that is not mate, ask one question: **can Black still make a legal move?** If Black has no legal move and is not in check, the game is a draw, however much material you have.

steps.caption: White to move: mate in three. The checks Qg5+ and Qh5+ only draw.

line.say: A quiet queen move, a knight's move from the king, with no check.
Another quiet queen move. The white king stays on f3.
The white king guards g4, so the queen mates.

steps.text: **Three checks before every move.** 1. If it is not mate, can Black's king still move? 2. Can the king capture your piece for free? 3. Is your own king close enough to protect the final check? A move that takes the last square without giving check is stalemate. Now one look-alike: the same queen move, one king step apart.

steps.title: Same queen move, one king step apart
steps.prompt: White plays Qg6 in both. Black's king is on h7 or on h8. Predict the result each time, then check.
Which of your checks (Black's legal moves, the safety of your piece, your king's distance) did you skip before a move? What will you check first next time?
